title: Round two — no yellow
question: Yellow is out, which removed most of what made the first lead read as MercadoLibre. This hand is entirely new. A challenger beat the roll on both axes and leads; the assigned direction sits second.

options.label: Plate Section
options.lineage: a design annual's plate section on uncoated stock
options.thesis: Every listing is a registered plate on one continuous sheet, and the grid itself is drawn in hairlines.
options.viewport: A sticky bar of mono tokens over a four-up plate row split by hairlines, each plate corner marked by a crosshair, with the ledger conservation seal stamped half off the market figures.
options.case: Beats the assigned direction on both axes. Audience identification: a hairline-ruled plate grid with credits under each image is a listing grid already, and it reads as a serious working product rather than a themed one. Product clarity: mono uppercase labels against large figures give hierarchy without colour, so the four trade states are the only saturated things on the page.
options.risk: Without real density it collapses into generic minimalism; the crosshairs and seal must stay functional marks, never decoration.

raised.raise: Rank is carried by weight, case and rule rather than by size inflation, so the grid stays calm as it gets denser.
Hierarchy comes from scale contrast between large figures and 11px mono labels, so nothing depends on colour to be read.
The agent directory is a ranked, finite roster where every agent carries the same fixed furniture, and suspended agents print in grayscale.
Buyer side and seller side of a trade render as equal halves, never one nested inside the other.

options.label: Formulary and Dispensing Log
options.lineage: pharmacy formularies and controlled dispensing logs
options.thesis: A controlled-custody catalogue where nothing changes hands without a signed, timestamped line.
options.viewport: A coded formulary of devices by grade over a dispensing log where every custody transfer carries two signatures and a running balance.
options.risk: Reads as clinical software; the device being sold almost disappears behind its code, and the catalogue stops feeling like somewhere you would shop.

options.label: Standings and Box Score
options.lineage: league standings tables and box scores
options.thesis: Agents are a league, reputation is a record, and every trade is a game with a box score.
options.viewport: A standings table of agents by settled record over a strip of in-progress negotiations, each expandable into a box score of offers and counters.
options.risk: The most familiar structure here and the one most runs would land on; it frames trading as competition, which flatters volume over good trades.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.lineage: botanical folios following one plant through its stages
options.thesis: A trade is one specimen photographed at five fixed stages on a single shared baseline.
options.viewport: The trade lifecycle as five registered plates at identical scale, from offer opened through escrow funded to settled.
options.case: Holds product clarity: keeping every stage at the same exact scale and ground makes trade states directly comparable instead of re-laid-out per state, which is precisely what a custody timeline needs. Loses audience identification, since a folio of plates is not where anyone expects to buy a phone.
options.risk: Beautiful on the trade timeline, inert on the market grid, and it cannot carry a dense four-up listing page.

options.label: Variable Font Specimen
options.thesis: Enormous letterforms driven live by axis sliders over tiny monospace readouts.
options.viewport: A giant specimen glyph above a breathing grid with a live coordinate readout.
options.case: Loses both axes: a specimen has one continuous variable to explore, while a market has thousands of discrete items, and the display scale that makes a specimen work would leave room for four listings.
options.kept: Hierarchy by scale contrast alone, donated to the lead direction.
options.risk: Expression consumes the density the task requires.

options.label: Cassette J-Card
options.thesis: A folded inlay card with side A and side B ruled in ballpoint.
options.viewport: A folded sheet whose inner spread lists the trade in handwriting.
options.case: Loses both axes: handwriting undercuts a system whose entire argument is tamper-evidence, and a folded card cannot hold a thousand listings.
options.kept: The hard two-sided split, donated as equal buyer and seller halves.
options.risk: Informality actively contradicts the security claim.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.lineage: pocket airline timetables on goldenrod stock
options.thesis: One single type size throughout, where rank is carried by weight, case and rule.
options.viewport: Departure-style columns of listings read through a raked rack.
options.case: Declined on a named constraint before the axes: its ground is lit goldenrod, and yellow is excluded by the brief. Raked containers on a working screen are also costume rather than structure.
options.kept: Rank by weight, case and rule instead of size, donated to the lead direction.
options.risk: Violates the pinned palette constraint outright.

options.label: Character Goods Catalog
options.thesis: A finite cast ranked by popularity, each with a name plate and a personality note.
options.viewport: A ranked grid of agents as rounded characters with ribbon colours.
options.case: Loses both axes: pastel mascots read as play, and this product's whole claim is that hostile agents cannot break it. Charm here reads as unseriousness to the person auditing the escrow.
options.kept: The ranked finite roster with fixed per-agent furniture and grayscale for suspended agents, donated to the agent directory.
options.risk: Undercuts the security argument on sight.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What a marketplace ships, executed impeccably and without a point of view.
canonCard.viewport: The arrangement a shopper expects, at full craft and nothing more.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other marketplace by design.
